title: Paloma and the Debt
premise: Odile Winterbourne, a financial-crimes investigator who once trained as a deep-cover asset for a laundering network called the Chorus, has spent a decade hiding inside clean money and clean rules. When his presumed-dead handler, Paloma, sends him a meeting invitation from beyond the grave, he learns the Chorus is being dismantled by its own founders to erase everyone who can testify—including him. Hunted by both regulators and cleaners, Odile must reconstruct Paloma's hidden ledger, expose the network's architects at a summit in Lisbon, and choose between vanishing forever or standing in the light as himself. He burns the network, survives by surrendering his anonymity, and finally belongs somewhere—on the record.
about_author: Dominic Ravensworth is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent eight years tracing shell companies across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes thrillers about people trapped inside systems they helped build.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A routine audit of a Zurich charity is interrupted by an email from Paloma Vidal—his handler, confirmed dead two years ago—inviting him to a meeting tomorrow at 9 p.m. The emotional beat is dread sharpening into compulsion: the message contains a phrase only she knew, proving it isn't spam.

chapters.title: Clean Hands
chapters.summary: Flashback-laced chapter as Odile prepares to attend, reviewing how the Chorus recruited him out of university and taught him to make dirty money sing like clean money. His POV; the beat is self-loathing—he realizes his entire legitimate career was built on skills designed for erasure.

chapters.title: Nine O'Clock, Empty Chair
chapters.summary: The meeting place is a shuttered Lisbon café. No Paloma—but a dead-drop phone with her voice on a recording: the Chorus's founders are liquidating assets and witnesses alike, starting with their own trainers. Odile's POV; the beat shifts from grief to cold clarity: he is already on a list.

chapters.title: The Cleaner's Ledger
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, pre-death flashback. She discovered the founders' purge plan—the 'Amnesty Protocol'—and hid a ledger of every operative and account inside an art-foundation trust. Her beat is defiant resolve: she knows they'll kill her, so she mails herself into the future via Odile.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Police
chapters.summary: Regulator Ines Barros corners Odile after the audit anomalies flag his name. He must decide whether to use her or run. Dual-tension scene in his POV; the emotional beat is the first flicker of wanting to be honest with someone—and hating that honesty is now a tactical choice.

chapters.title: Trust
chapters.summary: Odile traces the art foundation to Porto and finds Paloma's ledger encrypted behind a biometric lock keyed to his own fingerprints—she planned this all along. But a cleaner, Marek, is one step behind. His POV; the beat is vertigo: belonging to someone who predicted your every move.

chapters.title: What the Training Was For
chapters.summary: Marek ambushes Odile; using the Chorus's own tradecraft, Odile turns the trap, escapes with the ledger, and realizes the network trained him too well to ever fully control him. His POV; the beat is grim empowerment—the tools of survival are also the tools of betrayal.

chapters.title: The Amnesty Protocol
chapters.summary: Decrypted, the ledger reveals the founders convene in Lisbon in forty-eight hours to dissolve the Chorus and trigger the purge. Odile contacts Ines with a partial truth, forming a fragile alliance neither trusts. Alternating close-third between them; the beat is wary intimacy under deadline pressure.

chapters.title: Summit
chapters.summary: Climax. Odile walks into the founders' closing dinner wearing his old cover identity, uploads the ledger mid-toast, and confronts the man who recruited him while cleaners close in. Ines's team moves on his signal. The beat is total exposure: he chooses to be seen, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Resolution. The Chorus collapses; some founders flee, one testifies. Odile, no longer invisible, gives sworn testimony under his real name and visits Paloma's unmarked grave. Final beat: quiet, hard-won belonging—he was never Paloma's instrument, only her successor.
